title: Longwall Top-Coal Caving for Indian Thick Seams: Geotechnical Feasibility and a Safety-Assurance Framework for the Godavari Valley Coalfield
content: Longwall top-coal caving (LTCC) can increase recovery from thick seams; however, its performance in overseas mines does not establish transferability to Indian coal measures. This critical integrative review combines peer-reviewed LTCC research, published and technical evidence from the Godavari Valley Coalfield (GVCF), and the statutory and safety evidence needed for controlled implementation in India. The synthesis evaluates top-coal failure and draw, first top-coal caving distance (FTCD), seam and stone-band variability, roof behaviour, in-situ stress, roadway orientation, support response, gas, spontaneous heating, and commissioning controls. Available measurements indicate a broadly north-east–south-west maximum horizontal stress direction in parts of the GVCF, with material local variation; Adriyala experience further indicates that roadway orientation can alter guttering, convergence, and reinforcement demand. Earlier GVCF screening produced divergent cavability and recovery estimates under Chinese and CSIRO-derived approaches, demonstrating model-form uncertainty rather than proving feasibility. The paper therefore proposes a staged evidence-to-decision framework linking regional screening, block qualification, three-dimensional characterisation, calibrated continuum–discontinuum modelling, multi-hazard assessment, an instrumented pilot, and independent review before expansion. LTCC is assessed as conditionally promising for selected GVCF blocks, but not demonstrated at coalfield scale. The principal limitation is the absence of an Indian LTCC production panel for calibration and the heterogeneous accessibility and quality of regional data.
